statement: The biography gives the premiership as 24 July 2019 to 6 September 2022.
locator: Biography
limits: Chronology agrees with separately retrieved UK Parliament career record V01.

statement: The Court held the advice to prorogue Parliament unlawful and the resulting prorogation null and without effect.
locator: [2019] UKSC 41, paragraphs 50, 61 and 69–70
limits: Checked the Court’s own conclusion and remedy, paragraphs 61 and 69–70, rather than allegations in the procedural history. No criminality or inferred motive is admitted.

statement: The Committee concluded that Johnson deliberately misled the House. The summary records its reasoning, his denials and his response to provisional conclusions.
locator: Summary, paragraphs 11–17
limits: The summary supports the attributed Committee conclusion. June 2023 committee conduct is outside the premiership. Full representations and Commons disposition remain outside this bounded verification.

statement: The committees identified both vaccination successes and serious weaknesses in the early pandemic response, including delayed lockdown and shortcomings affecting vulnerable groups.
locator: Opening summary and principal findings
limits: Both strengths and weaknesses are present in the official inquiry announcement. This verifies the summary, not all claims in the full report or personal prime ministerial responsibility.

statement: The government recorded Johnson’s Kyiv visit and announced additional military assistance and World Bank lending guarantees.
locator: Paragraphs describing assistance and lending guarantees
limits: The announcement records military aid and guarantees. Delivery and effect have not been independently established by this release.

statement: The retrieved biography states that Starmer was Prime Minister from 5 July 2024 to 20 July 2026.
locator: Biography
limits: Both boundaries agree with UK Parliament career record V02. This is cross-checking two institutional records, not certification of every biography statement.

statement: The announcement sets out monthly publication of ministerial gifts and hospitality, including values, and an independent adviser’s power to initiate investigations without a prime ministerial veto.
locator: Gifts and hospitality rules; independent adviser powers
limits: The dated announcement supports monthly disclosure and the no-veto investigation provision. Enforcement and actual compliance remain unverified.

statement: The register includes Arsenal tickets and hospitality received on 17 August 2024 and declared on 10 September 2024. Other entries concern earlier dates or periods straddling the start of the premiership.
locator: Category 3; Arsenal entry received 17 August 2024; accommodation entry 29 May–13 July 2024
limits: The Arsenal entry confirms receipt/acceptance on 17 August and registration on 10 September. Other benefits predate office or straddle it; no breach finding is inferred.

statement: The publication record identifies the Plan for Change and states it was presented to Parliament on 5 December 2024.
locator: Details and document metadata: CP 1210, ISBN 978-1-5286-5291-9
limits: Publication date, CP number and presentation to Parliament are confirmed on the landing page. The attachment is not represented as substantively reviewed.

statement: Starmer condemned violent disorder, referred to targeted Muslim and other minority communities, and stated that the government would support the police and pursue criminal enforcement.
locator: Speech transcript, paragraphs on targeted communities and policing
limits: The transcript supports the limited description of words delivered. Operational outcomes and effects on communities remain outside this source’s proof.

statement: The Treasury announced expanded Winter Fuel Payment eligibility in England and Wales using a £35,000 income threshold, following the narrower arrangements introduced for winter 2024/25.
locator: Eligibility announcement and Further background
limits: Treasury announcement confirms the threshold and the narrower 2024/25 background. Attribution to Starmer’s personal reasoning remains unsupported.

statement: The inspection identified serious weaknesses in victim service, crime recording, investigation and governance, while recognising some improvements and a programme of change.
locator: Printed pages 8–12: summary, supervision and governance, causes of concern; inspection conducted September–October 2020
limits: The report confirms the September–October 2020 inspection and adverse as well as qualifying findings. Footer confirms December 2020, but an exact publication day is not established.

statement: The police force announced removal from enhanced monitoring and described improvements in call handling, recording and investigation.
locator: Opening announcement and crime-recording/investigation passages
limits: The institutional account is now corroborated on the narrow removal-from-monitoring decision by the inspector’s original letter V05. Other performance figures and personal credit remain separately unverified.

statement: The archival biography records Obama’s inauguration on 20 January 2009 and return to private life on 20 January 2017.
locator: Political Career and Post-Presidency
limits: Only the inauguration and return-to-private-life dates were used. No other biographical claim is admitted through this verification.

statement: GAO identified inadequate CMS planning and oversight, increased contract costs and delayed functionality. The record includes agency responses and later implementation of recommendations.
locator: What GAO Found; Recommendations for Executive Action
limits: GAO highlights confirm planning and oversight weaknesses, cost increases and delayed functionality. Dynamic follow-up records implemented recommendations; that is separate from the 2014 original finding.

statement: The Board recommended ending bulk telephone-record collection, citing legal, privacy and effectiveness concerns. The report includes separate statements by two members.
locator: Printed page 16, Recommendation 1; introduction and annex contents
limits: Recommendation 1 supports the attributed legal/privacy/value concerns; contents identify separate member statements. They must be read before treating the conclusions as unanimous. This is not a judicial criminal finding.

statement: Obama set out announced intelligence reforms and further privacy work, presenting the need to balance security and civil liberties.
locator: Speech, reform proposals and closing discussion of privacy review
limits: Reform announcements and privacy work are in the 17 January speech. The speech predates the 23 January PCLOB report and is not described as a response to it.

statement: At the Newtown vigil Obama acknowledged bereaved families, praised responders and community support, and committed to work on preventing further shootings.
locator: Speech at Newtown High School, passages on families and prevention
limits: Transcript confirms the limited account of acknowledgement, praise and commitments. Empathy over the whole term and prevention outcomes are not established.

statement: The catalogue identifies the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act as Public Law 111–148, dated 23 March 2010.
locator: Content Details
limits: GovInfo catalogue confirms law identifier and 23 March 2010 date. No substantive statutory or implementation conclusion is inferred from metadata.

statement: The analysis reports changes in health insurance coverage and other indicators, and warns that numerical changes do not determine presidential credit or blame.
locator: Analysis introduction and Health Insurance section
limits: The analysis discusses insurance indicators and explicitly cautions against automatic presidential credit/blame. Original datasets and causal attribution remain outstanding.

statement: The government records Scholz’s election, appointment and oath as Federal Chancellor on 8 December 2021.
locator: Change of government; Bundestag elects Scholz; oath
limits: Official dated appointment/oath record supports 8 December 2021. An oath is not evidence that every duty was fulfilled.

statement: The official record documents the handover from Scholz to Merz on 6 May 2025 and includes their statements.
locator: Dated introduction and handover statements
limits: Dated handover record supports 6 May 2025 and observable transfer conduct. Ceremonial statements do not establish consistent humility.

statement: Scholz announced a security-policy shift following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, including a defence fund, commitments to allies and measures on energy security and household pressures.
locator: Fourth policy area: defence capability; energy security and relief package
limits: Official English text supports the announced defence fund, allied commitments and energy/household measures. Delivery is not established. German wording still requires review for any contested phrase.

statement: Reuters reported the budget ruling’s consequences and recorded Scholz’s stated intention to revise the relevant economic plan.
locator: Updated 15 November 2023; report opening and Scholz response
limits: Byline, displayed initial/update dates and quoted plan revision are confirmed. The underlying ruling is now checked against OS04 and V06; multiple syndicated versions would not count as independent origins.

statement: The GMCA notice states that the mayoral vacancy occurred on 19 June 2026 after Burnham’s election as an MP.
locator: Vacancy notice, published 19 June 2026
limits: Previously inaccessible page now retrieved directly. It gives the vacancy date as 19 June 2026 and was published that day. The start date is separately supported by V03.

statement: The independent review records that Burnham commissioned it and prioritised the experiences of bereaved families and other affected people.
locator: Sections 1.2–1.3, printed pages 11–12
limits: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

statement: The report records some respondents’ positive accounts of personal visits by the mayor and chief constable.
locator: Section 2.22, printed pages 49–50
limits: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

statement: The report also records that some respondents outside Manchester felt overlooked or less well supported. This is not a finding of Burnham’s sole responsibility.
locator: Section 2.23, printed page 50
limits: PDF now retrieved. Sections 1.2–1.3 establish commissioning and intended family participation. Section 2.22 records positive visit experiences; section 2.23 records perceived geographical gaps in support. These accounts do not establish representativeness or sole mayoral responsibility.

statement: GMCA records Burnham’s decision to introduce bus franchising in March 2021, with the first services running in September 2023 and final rollout in January 2025.
locator: The journey to franchised bus services
limits: Official overview now retrieved. It records the March 2021 decision and rollout dates. Its budget, patronage and comparative claims are not independently validated here.

statement: The Court’s press release states that the Second Supplementary Budget Act 2021 was incompatible with specified Basic Law provisions and void; the operative judgement confirms this.
locator: Press release opening; V06 operative judgement
limits: Previously inaccessible press release now retrieved. Its operative account agrees with the separately retrieved judgement V06. Invalid legislation is not a finding of personal dishonesty.
